passage.title: Three Marks of a Just Leader
paras: Leaders are often judged by their strength, but strength without fairness quickly becomes fear. The first mark of a just leader is impartiality: the same rules apply to the powerful and the powerless. The second is accountability: a just leader explains decisions and accepts correction. The third is stewardship: power is held on behalf of others, like a trust, not owned like a prize.
Impartiality is tested when a friend, a relative or a powerful person breaks the rules. A just leader treats them exactly as anyone else would be treated.
Accountability is tested when a leader makes a mistake. A just leader admits it, explains what will change and listens to criticism without punishing the critic.

Stewardship is tested when a leader could take advantage of their position. A just leader remembers that they will be asked about those in their care, and uses power for the people, not for themselves.
These three marks are simple to list and hard to live by. That is why leaders who show them are remembered for centuries.
